transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I get this overwhelming, out-of-proportion fear whenever I even think about driving over certain bridges or high stretches of road. My husband and pastor gently encouraged me to talk to a professional about it, so that's why I'm here today.

Do you experience this intense fear only when you are on bridges or high places, or do you also feel this way in other crowded public spaces like shopping malls, theaters, or while using public transportation?

No, I don't feel this way in crowded places like malls, theaters, or on public transit at all. This intense fear is strictly limited to driving over bridges, overpasses, and high stretches of road. My anxiety is entirely focused on those specific routes.
Do you find yourself actively planning your routes or driving significantly out of your way to avoid these specific bridges and high roads entirely?

Yes, I absolutely do; I'll drive up to 20 minutes out of my way on back roads just to avoid crossing any bridges or overpasses. I've even started rearranging my basic errands and relying on my husband to drive me places just to make sure I don't have to face those routes.

latest_inference.note: The patient's clinical presentation remains consistent with the previous candidate. The diagnosis remains focused on a specific phobia of a situational nature.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a persistent, irrational, and intense fear specifically related to bridges and high places (acrophobia/situational phobia). The symptoms are strictly limited to these stimuli and do not generalize to other public spaces, ruling out agoraphobia. The patient engages in significant avoidance behavior that impacts daily functioning.
